This semi-automatic marksman rifle is designed to operate at extremely long ranges.

Since it's hard to see that far due to the Mist, this unscoped version was made for use at shorter distances.

This semi-automatic marksman rifle is designed to operate at the limit of the range one can see within the Mist.

As such, only the most calculating and patient use this weapon – and they often have a spotter.

A tactical submachine gun with reduced recoil, a high rate of fire, and an unusual magazine which is tricky to reload. Perfect for kicking down the few doors still standing in Zalesye.

This pristine model offers even better recoil, accuracy and durability... And goes through your ammo in seconds.

A fluid-filled sac that bursts on impact, spilling a burning slime used by Woundworts to dissolve aggressors.
Handle with care — or don’t handle at all.
A pre-War pocket gospel book, containing texts which are apparently very important for Acolytes and their Church.
A stash of supplies that an Acolyte must've been carrying somewhere.
Bits of robes and undergarments from the dedicated Acolytes, just as modest as the lives they lead.
High-quality Esmarch bandages from a well-maintained, pre-War kit.
A case of pro-grade tools for repairing any weapon from any state. Worth a lot.

This war-proven medkit has outlived both its owner and their country.

Can’t shake the feeling that I shouldn’t use it lightly.

Rodion – I had to leave for the Cemetery up north. Please drop by.

Grigory might have a cheap weapon for you to buy so you can make your way here. He's southwest of the Hospital, as usual.
- Alexei
Spent ammo casings, with burns and scratches that echo someone else's battles.

To the scavenger: I have gone to study the anomalous energy flux right down the road. Bring the toolbox there.
- Anatoly

To the scavenger: I have gone to study the anomalous energy flux right down the road. Bring the toolbox there.
- Anatoly

A rusty plate of armor which can be strapped to one's chest, offering minimal protection in combat.

If it stops even one bullet, that's already good enough.

A sorry bunch of rags with some improvised armored plating strapped to them. Better than nothing, but not enough to stop a bullet.

Many scavengers and highwaymen start off their careers with this sort of scrapped-together attire.

A detector for the Core of different Aspects.

Highly specialized equipment which serves only the bravest and most suicidal of Vultures.

A very common piece of headwear throughout Zalesye, and one of the first trades people make when they come into some money.

Its comfy shape and texture are great against the cold, but don't offer much protection.

Tongue from a dangerous Goyan creature, or "Sucker". Its long shape and sliminess make it feel like it's still alive...

Don't wanna be near this thing, much less carry it around.
A brown backpack made of leather and nylon, relatively comfortable and durable.
A tactical submachine gun with reduced recoil, a high rate of fire and an unusual magazine which is tricky to reload. Perfect for kicking down the few doors still standing in Zalesye.
A tactical submachine gun with reduced recoil, a high rate of fire, and an unusual magazine which is tricky to reload. Perfect for kicking down the few doors still standing in Zalesye.

A tactical submachine gun with reduced recoil and a high rate of fire. The unusual magazine from the 918 was replaced with a more standard one, less prone to jamming.

If that makes it more "reliable" or more "boring" depends on the individual.

A drink so tasty it makes you forget about the surrounding hellscape!
Well... That didn't last long. Time for some more.
One of the most common pieces of Pre-War soldier equipment, this cheaply mass-produced helmet is sturdy enough against bludgeon attacks, but will not stop a bullet.

These tattered bandages look like they’ll infect my wounds rather than protect them.

Still, it’s better than nothing – and I’ve used worse.
This should teach me to craft Bandages.
Acolytes careless w/ supplies. You find anything else, take it to the East camp.
A set of clothes from local Bandits. Surprisingly appropriate for running around and shooting people.
A barrel full of sacks of agricultural lime, which farmers use to help fertilize the soil. Heavy and cumbersome.
Used by scavengers to fix poorly maintained pre-War weaponry. Useful in a pinch.

The extracted fang of a bat. Were these animals always poisonous, or is that because of the Mist and radiation?

Gives me the creeps.

A very tasty (and expensive) soup made from beans, berries and meat.

The stew is so thick that I’m more than full by the time I finish eating. Makes me drowsy.
Berries from a joint Commonfolk and Rada farm. A bit... Small.

Mudlarks created this dish that only a few merchants dared taste.

They believe it enhances one’s awareness of the Mist...
A large filter for some sort of liquid; most likely an automobile part.
A pair of well-made, pre-War binoculars that have resisted the years. The casing is banged up, but the lenses have been preserved.

A semi-automatic shotgun that fans of the Mikhail series will be very comfortable with. Good for close ranges – breaching rooms, turning corners and blowing up limbs. Just gotta remember to hold it real tight.

A tasty drink to get your mind off the horrors all around!
Gives a performance boost too. Now, where to find some more?

This freakish gun is a home-brew combination of parts from different guns that were lost to history.

Terrible accuracy, powerful shots, and noise that will be heard across the wastes.

This bread is hard on the teeth and it tastes like ashy mold.

I power through each slice because I know it gives me energy.

Filthy old rags worn by most Commonfolk of Zalesye.

A reminder that, even after the apocalypse, there's no time wasted in finding the lowest common denominator.
A common butcher's knife, reappropriated for field use out of desperation. The wooden handle is rotting off.
A great condiment which goes with any meal. Hard to make, rare to come by, and it goes bad pretty fast.

The world used to be so beautiful that it was worth recording and revisiting. 

The thought lingers as I struggle to connect it with this broken camera husk.

These canned beans are the slop that’s kept me alive all these years.

Can’t even smell or taste them anymore, but they get me through the day.

This canned tuna meat has a suspiciously distant expiration date.

Good for me. It’s one of the tastier and most energy-filled rations out there.

The water around here has a taste. The implication isn’t good.

I should drink this in small swigs throughout the day – lessen the risk of radiation poisoning.

A big and heavy battery, probably drained but still worth something.

Can't imagine how it'd be to see all these vehicles moving.
A chemical container for hazardous materials. Must have seemed like a big deal before the Mist.

A bloody chest patch that could have been given out by folks at the Hospital, or could be homemade.

The only protection it offers is to stop a wound that's already bleeding.

A time-tested drug which at once relaxes and keeps us alert.

Not even the Mist can prevent a Vulture from taking these out in the middle of a scavenge.
A bundle of rags worn by the common men and women of Zalesye. The low quality cloth makes them even more vulnerable than they already are.

This tool is mostly useful for clearing out debris, helping crafty scavengers search buildings more easily.

They can also be used as a last resort in combat.

These berries are a common find in every region I’ve traveled.

They grow even in areas full of Mist, but how this affects the fruit, I don’t know.

A diamond ring which probably symbolized some sort of love or marriage. 

Priceless before the War; could someone in Zalesye still be interested?

Old documents that miraculously survived the War and the Mist.

They seem very trivial and bureaucratic in nature.
This ear from a mutated hound has a bunch of cartilage which is actually quite useful for medicinal purposes.

Skin from a Drekavac hound, used for clothes and shelter.

Don't stick around when they're tanning it, shit smell.

A Palatine's dog tag with the name "Ilich", brought all the way here from the Scrapyard.
Found near his corpse, and just as cold.

These dried mushrooms are specially prepared to give psychoactive effects.

They’ve been dulled by age, but I should still be careful when I eat this.

While I think I could find rocks that are juicier than this, the nutrition here is undeniable.

Just gotta make sure I have the time when I take this out to chew it.

A reliable dust coat is an important part of a Scavenger’s attire, since it protects against the unpredictable weather, dust and debris of the areas near the Thresholds.

Although there is not much variety to be found in this category, it’s still very important to keep one’s dust coat relatively clean and in one piece.

A Mechanist's bizarre invention, the Ekzoskelet Legs are a heavy-duty lining of metal parts woven together with regular trousers.

They're designed to offer great resistance and to actually improve the wearer's stamina, but they're still very clumsy to use.
A bundle of electric wires that should be reasonably valuable for a Mechanist.

An empty bottle, containing only the despair of alcoholic Commonfolk.

I hear even some pre-War people used to collect tare for money.
A spore that grows on cereal and grains. Toxic and hallucinogenic. Needs careful preparation before use for opening my third eye or something like that.
A big case of high-grade tools for critical repairs. Having one of these can be life-saving.
Mutants have many teeth. Not that valuable in the market.

A jagged, yellowed fang torn from the mouth of the beast known as Veles. Still slick with the scent of blood and Mist.

Carried as a badge of honor by experienced combatants – or by lunatics who believe it grants them the power of Mist.
A spool of threads used to stich together broken armor bits and fabric.

An eccentric fish soup that’s definitely an acquired taste.

The secret is to cook it for so long that it’s almost not radioactive at all.
A flamethrower designed for war, which saw little practical use. It's unwieldy, but deadly at close range.

Information of some sort used to be stored in these, but I don’t know how. 

Lots of things we used to know have been unlearned; what was the point?

A dusty book that predates even the War by at least a century.

It speaks of ideologies and History, but uses different languages at the same time. I can't read it.

A luxury food found throughout Zalesye. Great taste, not much nutrition.

I enjoy cheese more than other people seem to. Makes me almost emotional.

Fresh mushrooms with little to no radiation. Tasty, chewy and nutritious – a rare find.

These mushrooms can have drug-like effects when properly dried.
A small tub of glue used to quickly patch holes in clothing. Useful to have while out in the field.
A gold chain, meant to adorn one's neck. Should be a valuable trade, even if they just melt it down to get the gold.

This widespread Gas Mask was issued to Civil Defense and civilians alike, during the times of War. 

Vultures and Bandits often wear these for days at a time, and the mask’s straps dig themselves painfully into the back of their heads.
A piece of gray cloth; decent fabric, very nondescript.
Old rags worn by the people of Zalesye. They're sturdy enough to resist the harsh weather, but don't provide much warmth.
A piece of cloth that's been dyed green; an unusual color, but it's good-quality cloth.

A bunch of dirty rags, dyed green at a distant point in time; they offer no protection and very little warmth.

These clothes might be valued solely for their extra bit of color. Those who want to stand out for whatever reason may resort to something like this.

A complex mixture of drugs which can be quickly injected and discarded to numb pain, increase adrenaline and get me out of desperate situations.
This extra-sturdy, plated armor seems good enough to hold back a crowd of people, and even withstand some fire. It is heavy and difficult to wear, but survival is worth a little struggle.
A Mechanist's bold creation, weaving metal parts in and out of a regular, weathered blouse. They offer great resistance without sacrificing stamina.
A quality overcoat with some extra armor plating on the shoulder. The preferred gear for most scavengers, as it's very resistant to weather and the mud and grime of Zalesye.
